summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments, specifically a greptile P1 flagging an AAD generation mismatch in the bin restore path of the CipherBox SDK.
summary.outcome: Confirmed the P1 was valid: `bin/index.ts` was using `publishedNode.generation` instead of `childRef.generation` for AEAD construction at lines 330 and 360. Both were fixed, all 210 SDK unit tests passed, and the fix was committed and pushed.

repo: AAD for child read key seal/unseal MUST use `childRef.generation` (the parent mirror field on `SealedChildRef`), NOT `childPublished.generation` from the live envelope — a stale-CID serve causes GCM auth to fail closed (documented in navigate.ts §2.6 Pitfall 1).
`id` and `kind` are immutable across generations and correctly stay sourced from `publishedNode`, matching the `moveItem` convention in client.ts.
`moveItem` in client.ts and `navigate.ts:154-162` are the canonical reference implementations for AAD construction — new code in bin/index.ts must mirror them.

code.finding: Was using `publishedNode.generation` for AAD; must use `childRef.generation` (the parent mirror) to match the sealed key's binding.
Generation witness for the captured key must also use `childRef.generation`, not the live published generation, so `restoreFromBin` re-seals correctly at line 455.
Explicitly documents the AAD rule: childRef.generation (parent mirror) must be used, not childPublished.generation. Acts as the canonical spec comment for this invariant.
`moveItem` uses `destEntry.generation` (SealedChildRef field) for AAD, taking only id/kind from the live envelope — reference pattern for bin/index.ts.
`SealedChildRef.generation` is documented as a 'staleness witness mirror'; authoritative value lives on the child's own published envelope, but AAD binding must use the mirror.

workflow: Greptile P1 crypto findings should be traced through multiple call sites (seal, unseal, moveItem, navigate) before accepting or rejecting — the invariant was non-obvious from the bug site alone.
Running the targeted bin suite (21 tests) first, then the full SDK suite (210 tests) as a regression gate, is an efficient sequencing for scoped crypto fixes.

friction: The AAD generation invariant is only documented in navigate.ts comments and not enforced by types — required manual cross-referencing of three separate call sites (moveItem, navigate.ts, bin/index.ts) to confirm the bug.
open_items: The AAD generation rule (`childRef.generation` over `publishedNode.generation`) is currently only a comment convention — no type-level or lint enforcement exists to prevent future regressions in new seal/unseal sites.
